title: Created my first game ever!
author: No-Ear7072
selftext:
Heyy all!

I created my first war themed game ever! Everything I did (sounds, animations, textures assets etc) are created by AI.

I have been an avid gamer for all my life so just wanted to try something!

Let me know what you think please! Your feedback is much appreciated!

https://wrathofpasschendaele.vercel.app/

I hope you enjoy it!

comments.author: MoonBeamofEast
comments.body: Sorry for being harsh but stop wasting time by making AI slop and actually learn some gamedev skills, in current age its not that hard. You could literally buy FPS/TPS code from the asset store on discount and they will still run better than what you have made.

replies.author: No-Ear7072
replies.body: thank you for the reply! I am unfortunately not a game developer nor a coder. Everythingwas done using vibecoding with AI. I am sure there are a lot better tools out there

replies.author: MoonBeamofEast
replies.body: thanks for taking my comment in a positive manner, you will be surprised what you can do once you get your basics right, and it will be much cheaper than burning your tokens, good luck.

replies.author: jimukjxb
replies.body: Don't be disheartened and de-motivated by this guy's comment. Keep going.

comments.author: ArticleOrdinary9357
comments.body:
You’re wasting your time with all this ‘vibe-coding’ nonsense. It’s nowhere near good enough to make something really polished that can compete with real games made in a proper engine. Yes, those of us that can code/model etc are using AI where applicable and guess what …when the tools get better, it’ll be the people who know how to code and use the major engines that really  will be able to use them. ….vibecoding man. That phrase makes me want to kill somebody.

TL/DR: if you really want to make games. Learn an engine.

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body: I disagree with you about who will be the ones to win from AI, won't be the devs and designers, they don't understand systems within a business, it's going to be c suits and managers, also this isn't me having to at you or anything, just I've found my biggest source of truth has been those people not devs or designers they don't know shit.

replies.author: ArticleOrdinary9357
replies.body: Yeah, that makes no sense ….i mean it’s always some suit making the money but it’s still gonna be devs actually making the software however drastically ai changes the landscape. If your source of truth has been people telling you that you can make any kind of shippable product using just AI with the current technology than it isn’t really a source of truth.

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body:
That's because you don't understand the industry, before when someone would say E.g. make me a CRM for our company, you go research you find other CRMs you take parts company wants and you build it, normally everyday companies wouldn't be doing this cause the length time it take to create a vibe CRM take months, but with AI we can code it out super fast so changes how CRM is built you now building software that is dedicated to that company not CRM that fits many companies, so source of truth becomes the c-suit. The whole process is changing companies aren't buying into SaaS anymore they want internal apps to help increase value of the company, they also want tools that speed up production and most time SaaS has to much going on and missing parts that make life easier for the company. 

Does that make sense or you still don't understand. Give it to end of the year and companies will just vibe code their own tools its really not rocket science anymore.

replies.author: ArticleOrdinary9357
replies.body: Anyone who even consider a ‘vibe coded’ CRM or ERP system needs their brain jump started. We’re nowhere near that. And when we are, guess who will implement it?

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body: I don't think you understand what I am saying at all. This gone completely over your head, we must be at different levels.

replies.author: ArticleOrdinary9357
replies.body:
I’ve several pieces of software shipped and still working well after more than 5 years (small/medium ERPs/CRMs). I get what you’re saying about in-house software. But AI has not changed the reality that it is a HUGE money/resource drain and often ends in tears.

These things are complex and crucially, CONTEXT matters, which AI struggles with massively.

I work with a hugely complicated ERP/CRM system (essentially a SaaS, I’m sure you can guess which one) and thank god it is tried and tested for the most part AND I know there are always gonna be devs that are familiar with how the thing works.

We frequently have software packages and apps added to our toolset and if any of the developers mentioned the phrase ‘vibe coded’ they would be seen the door.

Many upper management or ‘C-suits’ as you call them are interested in AI because they think it can get rid of the software headache because they’ve seen some prototype web apps made with Claude and they couldn’t be more wrong (at this point in time)

You’re arguing that people with no technical background are the ‘source of truth’ on this stuff and it’s moronic ….and that is coming from a ‘c-suit’ by the way.
